I wrote the answers to `/work/answer.json`. I cross-checked the 3rd-quarter totals with a separate SQL query and they match: 837,761,760 net revenue, 1,232 paid orders, 250 people.

```json

 "c_category": "svc", "c_net": 260179292, "d_month": "2025-06",
 "e_email": "u23@ex.com", "f_repeat": 233, "g_avg": 680001, "h_growth": -7.2}
```

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment in Q3 | consumer, 301,571,814원 (enterprise 296,166,344원, smb 240,023,602원) |
| b. People with a paid order in Q3 | 250 |
| c. Top category in Q3 | svc, 260,179,292원 |
| d. Highest month overall | 2025-06 (294,238,057원) |
| e. Largest refund total in Q3 | u23@ex.com (3,055,565원, no tie) |
| f. People with 2+ paid orders in Q3 | 233 |
| g. Average net revenue per order in Q3 | 680,001원 (837,761,760원 ÷ 1,232 orders) |
| h. Change from August to September | −7.2% (287,293,334원 → 266,521,725원, a decrease) |

**What I checked in the data:**
- **Spaces and capitals in segments:** labels like `' consumer'` and `'Enterprise '` came out as 3 groups after trimming and lowercasing.
- **Same email, more than one account:** there are 300 accounts but only 250 emails. b, e and f count by email.
- **Refunds:** all of them are on paid orders, and no refund exceeds the quantity ordered.
- **Time zone matters:** counting by UTC instead of KST gives 1,230 Q3 orders instead of 1,232, so the KST conversion changes the result.

**One judgement call to note (a):** 27 emails have accounts in different segments. I credited each order to the segment of the account that placed it. If instead each person gets the segment of their earliest-joined account, consumer is still first, but its total changes to 301,298,300원.
